$comment: Packaged data: the brand-neutral default chart palette, as resolved sRGB hex for the light and dark themes. A host that wants its own colours declares a ChartPalette on its style profile; this file is only what a renderer draws in when none is declared. Hex, because the server-side chart renderer rasterises through resvg and cannot parse oklch(). The hues and steps are a published validated default categorical palette, used unchanged; only the slot ORDER is chosen here, so that slots 1-4 separate as a set (see `validated_slots$comment`). The roles under `light` and `dark` are the ChartPalette contract's own (`series`, `sequential`, `background`, `ink`, `muted`, `grid`, `rule`, `context`, `on_fill`) plus `highlight`. Changing any colour means re-running the checks pinned in tests/test_vega_render.py::TestPaletteArtifact, not editing one value.
series_slots$comment: How wide the categorical palette IS: the length of each theme's `series` list, and the ChartPalette contract's SERIES_SLOTS. Everything that needs the width reads this one key rather than a literal written somewhere else. Contrast `validated_slots`, which records where a MEASUREMENT stopped rather than how many colours there are.
validated_slots$comment: Where validated separation ENDS, not where the palette does. Slots 1-4 (blue, green, magenta, yellow) separate as a SET in both themes: every pair, not only neighbours, clears OKLab dE 6 under simulated protanopia and deuteranopia (13.0 light, 6.9 dark) and dE 15 under normal vision (19.6 light, 19.3 dark). Slots 5-8 (aqua, orange, violet, red) are a second tier: all eight clear dE 8 CVD and dE 15 normal-vision between NEIGHBOURS (worst 9.1/19.6 light, 8.4/19.3 dark) but not between every pair. Past 8 the renderers recycle from slot 1. None of those is a refusal to draw; what makes the second tier honest is that a direct label on every mark becomes mandatory at five series. Contrast against the chart surface: slot 1 clears 3:1 in both themes; slots 3-5 fall below 3:1 on the light surface, so a categorical colour must never be the only way a level is identified -- the one arm that draws categorical colour names every level in its values table.
